claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in high-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings is governed by the interaction between coherent lattice strain and diffusion-mediated dislocation glide.
Dislocation density is a structural mediator of the time-dependent plastic-deformation behavior.
Diffusion-mediated dislocation glide is an operative deformation mechanism under the proposed conditions.
Lattice-strain relaxation is an operative mechanism under the proposed conditions.
High-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings will exhibit a lower creep rate than compositionally similar conventional alloys without a multilayer structure.
High-entropy-alloy multilayer coatings will resist plastic deformation better than compositionally similar conventional alloys without a multilayer structure.
The proposed behavior applies over 500–700 °C and 100–500 MPa.
Outside some temperature and stress ranges, lattice strain and dislocation-glide mechanisms will no longer dominate the deformation behavior.
Dislocation density and lattice strain should correlate with the observed creep behavior.
